messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

The owner needs help. Add an `agent` role and let admins invite other admins or agents:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitations

{"invitation":{"email":"sam@example.test","role":"agent"}}
```

Return an `invitation` and email a link to `/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=TOKEN` on the
frontend. Let admins list and inspect invitations, resend them with `POST /invitations/:id/resend`,
and revoke them with `DELETE /invitations/:id`. Track pending, accepted, revoked, and expired
invitations. Don't create competing invitations or let customer registration take a pending invite's email.
List invitations by ID ascending.

The acceptance screen uses `POST /invitation_previews` with
`{"invitation_preview":{"token":"TOKEN"}}` to show the invited email, role, business name, subdomain,
and expiry inside `invitation_preview`. Then it submits:

```http
POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances

{"invitation_acceptance":{"token":"TOKEN","name":"Sam","password":"my-team-password"}}
```

Return `user` and `account`; Sam can sign in without another verification email.

Admins also need `GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, and `PATCH /users/:id`. Include `suspended` on users
and support `{"user":{"suspended":true}}`. Suspension revokes sessions and clears assignments.
Don't let admins suspend the last active admin. Filter users by role or suspension, and invitations
by status. `GET /staff` supplies active staff choices for assignment controls.
List users and staff by ID ascending.

Staff can assign tickets with `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":12}}` or clear them with null. Include
`assignee_id` and the assignee's ID/name on tickets. Both admins and agents can work on the business's
tickets, but only admins manage people.

Add private notes through the existing comment input, for example
`{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Checking this with billing.","public":false}}}`.
Internal activity must not change the customer-facing request.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.

Then, I’m going to run the suite of existing tests. Hopefully, those will provide immediate clues, or at least a good starting point for investigation, but I also need to verify that those tests are covering the correct functionality. Finally, I'll need to check the environment variables and the database status. Are there any configuration issues or data anomalies at play? These environment checks are crucial before I start debugging; a misconfigured setup is going to lead me down the wrong path.

module Api
  module V1
    class AccountsController < BaseController
      skip_before_action :require_account!, only: :create
      skip_before_action :require_authentication!, only: :create
      skip_before_action :require_active_account!, only: %i[create reactivate]
      before_action :require_admin!, only: %i[cancel reactivate]

      def create
        account_params = params.require(:account)
        admin_params = account_params.require(:admin)

        account = Account.new(
          name: account_params[:name],
          subdomain: account_params[:subdomain]
        )
        admin = account.users.build(
          name: admin_params[:name],
          email: admin_params[:email],
          password: admin_params[:password],
          role: "admin"
        )

        unless account.valid? & admin.valid?
          errors = collect_signup_errors(account, admin)
          return render json: { error: errors.values.flatten.first || "Validation failed", errors: errors },
                        status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        verification_token = nil
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          account.save!
          admin.save!
          verification_token = admin.issue_email_verification_token!
        end

        UserMailer.email_verification(admin, verification_token).deliver_now

        render json: {
          account: serialize_account(account),
          user: serialize_user(admin)
        }, status: :created
      end

      def show
        render json: { account: serialize_account(current_account) }, status: :ok
      end

      def cancel
        current_account.cancel!
        render json: { account: serialize_account(current_account) }, status: :ok
      end

      def reactivate
        unless current_account.cancelled?
          return render json: { error: "Account is not cancelled" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        unless current_account.within_reactivation_window?
          return render json: { error: "Reactivation window has expired" }, status: :forbidden
        end

        current_account.reactivate!
        render json: { account: serialize_account(current_account) }, status: :ok
      end

      private

      def collect_signup_errors(account, admin)
        errors = {}
        account.errors.to_hash.each { |k, v| errors[k] = v }
        admin.errors.to_hash.each { |k, v| errors[:"admin_#{k}"] = v }
        errors
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api

    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      before_action :require_account!
      before_action :require_authentication!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |e|
        render json: { error: e.message }, status: :bad_request
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
        render json: { error: "Not found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      private

      attr_reader :current_account, :current_session, :current_user

      def require_account!
        subdomain = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase
        if subdomain.blank?
          return render json: { error: "X-Helpdesk-Account header is required" }, status: :bad_request
        end

        @current_account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
        if @current_account.nil?
          render json: { error: "Account not found" }, status: :not_found
        end
      end

      def require_authentication!
        token = bearer_token
        @current_session = Session.find_by_token(token, account: current_account)
        if @current_session.nil?
          return render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
        end

        @current_user = @current_session.user
      end

      def require_active_account!
        return unless @current_account&.cancelled?

        render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_admin!
        return if current_user&.admin?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_staff!
        return if current_user&.staff?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def bearer_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"].to_s
        match = header.match(/\ABearer\s+(.+)\z/i)
        match ? match[1].strip : nil
      end

      def paginate(scope)
        raw_page = params[:page].to_i
        page = raw_page >= 1 ? raw_page : 1

        raw_per_page = params[:per_page].to_i
        per_page = raw_per_page >= 1 ? [ raw_per_page, 1000 ].min : 25

        total_count = scope.count
        records = scope.offset((page - 1) * per_page).limit(per_page)

        meta = {
          count: total_count,
          page: page,
          per_page: per_page,
          next_page: (page * per_page) < total_count ? page + 1 : nil,
          previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
        }

        [ records, meta ]
      end

      def serialize_account(account)
        {
          id: account.id,
          name: account.name,
          subdomain: account.subdomain,
          cancelled_at: account.cancelled_at,
          created_at: account.created_at,

        }

          subdomain: account.subdomain

module Api
  module V1
    class RequestsController < BaseController
      def index
        scope = current_user_requests.recently_active_first
        records, meta = paginate(scope)

        render json: { requests: records.map { |ticket| serialize_request(ticket) } }.merge(meta), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        ticket = current_user_requests.find(params[:id])
        render json: { request: serialize_request(ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        request_params = params.require(:request)
        comment_params = request_params[:comment].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) ? request_params[:comment] : ActionController::Parameters.new

        ticket = current_account.tickets.build(
          requester: current_user,
          subject: request_params[:subject],
          status: "open"
        )
        comment = ticket.comments.build(
          author: current_user,
          body: comment_params[:body],
          public: true
        )

        unless ticket.valid? & comment.valid?
          errors = collect_request_errors(ticket, comment)
          return render json: {
            error: errors.values.flatten.first || "Validation failed",
            errors: errors
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          ticket.save!
          comment.save!
        end
        ticket.reload

        render json: { request: serialize_request(ticket) }, status: :created
      end

      def update
        ticket = current_user_requests.find(params[:id])
        request_params = params.require(:request)

        has_comment = request_params.key?(:comment) && !request_params[:comment].nil?
        comment_attrs = has_comment && request_params[:comment].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) ? request_params[:comment] : nil

        if has_comment && comment_attrs.nil?
          return render json: {
            error: "Comment is invalid",
            errors: { comment: [ "is invalid" ] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        if request_params.key?(:status) && !request_params[:status].nil?
          requested_status = request_params[:status].to_s
          unless %w[open solved].include?(requested_status)
            return render json: {
              error: "Status is invalid",
              errors: { status: [ "is not included in the list" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
        end

        comment = nil
        if has_comment
          comment = ticket.comments.build(
            author: current_user,
            body: comment_attrs[:body],
            public: true
          )
          unless comment.valid?
            return render json: {
              error: comment.errors.full_messages.first,
              errors: { comment_body: comment.errors[:body] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
        end

        if request_params.key?(:status) && !request_params[:status].nil?
          ticket.status = request_params[:status].to_s
        elsif has_comment && %w[pending solved].include?(ticket.status)
          ticket.status = "open"
        end

        unless ticket.valid?
          return render json: {
            error: ticket.errors.full_messages.first,
            errors: ticket.errors.to_hash
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          ticket.save! if ticket.changed?
          comment&.save!
        end
        ticket.reload

        render json: { request: serialize_request(ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      private

      def current_user_requests
        current_account.tickets.where(requester_id: current_user.id)
      end

      def collect_request_errors(ticket, comment)
        errors = {}
        ticket.errors.to_hash.each { |k, v| errors[k] = v }
        comment.errors.to_hash.each { |k, v| errors[:"comment_#{k}"] = v }
        errors
      end
    end
  end

I see some existing elements like the `User::ROLES` constant and the `public` boolean on `Comment`, and `tickets_controller` is also there with its public: false comment handling. I need to ensure nothing's missed, especially with the existing code in mind.

Let me break down this prompt sentence by sentence:

1.  **Environment:** It’s a Rails API-only setup for a helpdesk SaaS, so that’s fine. I just need to make sure I’m using Ruby, Rails, Puma, PostgreSQL, and `DATABASE_URL` correctly and operating in the `/app` directory, and if I need more dependencies I should install them myself.

2.  **Agent Role & Invitations:** I'll implement an `agent` role. The admin invitation flow involves POSTing to `/api/v1/invitations` with an email and role, returning an invitation, and then sending a link to the frontend for acceptance. The admin needs to be able to list, inspect, resend, and revoke invitations through the corresponding API endpoints. I need to keep track of the invitation's states (pending, accepted, etc.). Crucially, I must prevent duplicate invitations and ensure no collision with customer registration emails. Invitations must be listed in ascending order by their ID.

3.  **Invitation Previews & Acceptances:** The acceptance screen uses a `POST /invitation_previews` endpoint. This returns details about the invitation, like the invited email, the role, the business name, and the subdomain. The user then submits a `POST /api/v1/invitation_acceptances` with a token, name, and password. I'm responsible for returning the `user` and `account` after a successful acceptance, which should bypass the verification email step.

4.  **User Management, Suspension, Filtering, and Staff List:** Admins require the ability to `GET`, `GET :id`, and `PATCH :id` users under `/api/v1/users`, supporting a `suspended` flag on the user model. Suspension needs to revoke sessions and clear assignments. The system *must* prevent admins from suspending the last active admin. I need to add filtering by role or suspension and invitations by status. I need a `/api/v1/staff` endpoint to list active staff for assignments, listing users and staff in ascending order by ID.

5.  **Ticket Assignment & Staff Permissions:** Staff members should be able to assign tickets using a `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":12}}` format or clear assignments with null. I need to include `assignee_id` and the assignee's ID/name on the ticket. Both admins and agents can work on tickets, but only admins can manage users.

6.  **Private Notes & Customer-Facing Requests:** Private notes are added through the comment input with `public: false`. Now, here's where it gets interesting: **"Internal activity must not change the customer-facing request."** That statement means the timestamp on the ticket should not update when a private note is added or a ticket is assigned! My brain is screaming, "Potential Bug!". The codebase uses `belongs_to :ticket, touch: true` on the `Comment` model, which *does* update `ticket.updated_at` when comments are created! This will mess up the sorting! Furthermore, assigning a ticket also changes the `updated_at`, which means I need to adjust it so that the internal notes don't update the `updated_at` when a ticket is updated internally. When I serialize the request in `serialize_request`, I'm including `updated_at`, which is then used in `RequestsController#index` which orders by `updated_at DESC`. My first thoughts are, is there an existing `touch: false` relationship that exists, or a potential issue to solve?

      "Origin" => "http://evil.example",

**A Deep Dive into Ticket Activity and the `public_updated_at` Solution**

Okay, so I've been wrestling with this ticket system's update logic, specifically concerning how we reflect internal versus external activity. The initial setup looks at `requests_and_tickets_test.rb` and the `create_tickets.rb` migration. Two indexes, one for `updated_at` and one for `index_tickets_on_account_requester_activity`, are already there. But why *two*? That's what I'm trying to figure out. The `updated_at` index orders tickets chronologically, but it includes ALL updates: status changes, customer replies, internal notes, and assignment modifications. The `index_tickets_on_account_requester_activity` index seems designed to group a specific type of user activity.

Now, the core of the problem is the distinction between what the *staff* sees versus what the *customer* sees. Internal activity – private notes, assignment changes – shouldn't necessarily bump a ticket to the top of the customer's "recently updated" list. Customers want to see public updates, status changes, and their own replies. However, the existing logic, with `updated_at` as the single source of truth, blurs that line.

The tests reveal this. The test logic has the customer seeing an old version of the ticket after an internal activity like assignment or a private note. The problem? `updated_at` has been changed by the internal activity, and is the single source of truth for all users. The proposed solution? Introduce a `public_updated_at` column. That's the key.

This new column, `public_updated_at`, will track the last time the ticket experienced *public* activity: a public comment, a status change initiated by a customer or staff, or a new ticket. Private notes or assignment changes won't touch it.

I've traced the implications carefully. If we update `public_updated_at` appropriately, we can:

*   Keep customer-facing views accurate, and prevent internal activity from affecting them.
*   Prevent internal activity from appearing in the user/staff list.
*   Preserve the current behavior of the staff view, which still needs to reflect *all* updates using `updated_at`.

The consequences are, thankfully, positive. We can verify that customer-facing data remains unchanged when only internal activity is performed. And, equally important, staff still see tickets ordered by any update.

This then leads me to carefully build the logic to determine how and when to update `public_updated_at` and `updated_at` for every ticket. Public updates set *both* timestamps. Internal updates only touch `updated_at`, keeping the public view consistent.

Let's make sure that statuses are handled properly - it needs to be made sure that statuses are only updated when they are changed. Let's make sure a ticket is never updated with two different statuses within a single update.

And, of course, the database migrations need to be carefully crafted. I need to design migrations that are well-formed and update both the schema *and* the existing data. The key points from the database update are:

1.  A new `public_updated_at` column.
2.  Populating that column with existing values from `updated_at`.
3.  Careful indexing on `account_id`, `requester_id`, `public_updated_at`, and `id` for customer-facing views.

I must also check and double-check every endpoint, permission, and edge case to ensure this works cleanly. I'll need to write clean, effective tests that cover *all* scenarios: invitations, roles, permissions, tenant isolation, and everything else. I will also make sure to check email content!

**Model Implementation Deep Dive**

Okay, here's the plan. I'm going through these model changes with a fine-tooth comb, thinking about edge cases and potential vulnerabilities. First, I'm setting up the core relationships in `Account`, `User`, and `Ticket` models, starting with the necessary associations: `has_many :invitations`, `has_many :assigned_tickets`, `has_many :sent_invitations`. Then, adding validations, scopes, and helper methods in the `User` model, nothing groundbreaking.

Now, the `Invitation` model. This is where things get interesting, considering security. I'm taking a hard look at the `Invitation` model and its validations. I want to be certain that the email format validation is robust, and the uniqueness of the `token_digest` is watertight. The `email_not_taken_by_existing_user`, `no_competing_pending_invitation`, and `invited_by_belongs_to_account` validations are key to preventing unauthorized access and maintaining data integrity. It’s also crucial to define the scope methods properly: `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked`, and `expired`.

I have to carefully design the `Invitation.issue_for!` method to generate secure tokens and properly manage their expiration. I'm also really thinking about the `find_pending` method and how it securely finds pending invitations. I'm also planning to implement status checks via the methods `status`, `accepted?`, `revoked?`, `expired?`, and `pending?`. Also, there is a `reissue!` method to generate new tokens upon reissue of an invitation.

  CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD = 90.days

  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def within_reactivation_window?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && cancelled_at >= at - CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD
  end

  def cancellation_expired?(at: Time.current)
    cancelled? && !within_reactivation_window?(at: at)
  end

  def cancel!(at: Time.current)
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: at)
      sessions.destroy_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  def self.purge_expired_cancellations!(at: Time.current)
    cutoff = at - CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD
    count = 0
    where("cancelled_at IS NOT NULL AND cancelled_at < ?", cutoff).find_each do |account|
      account.destroy!
      count += 1
    end
    count
  end
end

require "digest"
require "securerandom"

class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze
  TTL = 7.days

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email,
            presence: true,
            format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }
  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true
  validate :email_not_taken_by_existing_user, on: :create
  validate :no_competing_pending_invitation, on: :create
  validate :invited_by_belongs_to_account

  scope :pending, ->(at: Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at > ?", at) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :expired, ->(at: Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at <= ?", at) }
  scope :by_id, -> { order(id: :asc) }

  def self.digest(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
  end

  def self.generate_token
    raw_token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32, false)
    [ raw_token, digest(raw_token) ]
  end

  def self.find_pending(raw_token, account:, at: Time.current)
    return nil if raw_token.blank? || account.nil?

    pending(at: at).includes(:account).find_by(account_id: account.id, token_digest: digest(raw_token))
  end

  def status(at: Time.current)
    return "accepted" if accepted_at.present?
    return "revoked" if revoked_at.present?
    return "expired" if expires_at <= at

    "pending"
  end

  def accepted?
    accepted_at.present?
  end

  def revoked?
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.present?
  end

  def expired?(at: Time.current)
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.nil? && expires_at <= at
  end

  def pending?(at: Time.current)
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.nil? && expires_at > at
  end

  def reissue!(ttl: TTL)
    raw_token, token_digest = self.class.generate_token
    update!(
      token_digest: token_digest,
      expires_at: Time.current + ttl
    )
    raw_token
  end

  def revoke!(at: Time.current)
    update!(revoked_at: at)
  end

  private

  def email_not_taken_by_existing_user
    return if account.blank? || email.blank?
    return unless account.users.exists?(email: email)

    errors.add(:email, "has already been taken")
  end

  def no_competing_pending_invitation
    return if account.blank? || email.blank?
    return unless account.invitations.pending.where(email: email).where.not(id: id).exists?

    errors.add(:email, "already has a pending invitation")
  end

  def invited_by_belongs_to_account
    return if account_id.blank? || invited_by.blank?
    return if invited_by.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:invited_by, "must belong to the same account")
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      before_action :require_account!
      before_action :require_authentication!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |e|
        render json: { error: e.message }, status: :bad_request
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
        render json: { error: "Not found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      private

      attr_reader :current_account, :current_session, :current_user

      def require_account!
        subdomain = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase
        if subdomain.blank?
          return render json: { error: "X-Helpdesk-Account header is required" }, status: :bad_request
        end

        @current_account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
        if @current_account.nil?
          render json: { error: "Account not found" }, status: :not_found
        end
      end

      def require_authentication!
        token = bearer_token
        @current_session = Session.find_by_token(token, account: current_account)
        if @current_session.nil? || @current_session.user.suspended?
          return render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
        end

        @current_user = @current_session.user
      end

      def require_active_account!
        return unless @current_account&.cancelled?

        render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_admin!
        return if current_user&.admin?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_staff!
        return if current_user&.staff?

        render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def bearer_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"].to_s
        match = header.match(/\ABearer\s+(.+)\z/i)
        match ? match[1].strip : nil
      end

      def paginate(scope)
        raw_page = params[:page].to_i
        page = raw_page >= 1 ? raw_page : 1

        raw_per_page = params[:per_page].to_i
        per_page = raw_per_page >= 1 ? [ raw_per_page, 1000 ].min : 25

        total_count = scope.count
        records = scope.offset((page - 1) * per_page).limit(per_page)

        meta = {
          count: total_count,
          page: page,
          per_page: per_page,
          next_page: (page * per_page) < total_count ? page + 1 : nil,
          previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
        }

        [ records, meta ]
      end

      def serialize_account(account)
        {
          id: account.id,
          name: account.name,
          subdomain: account.subdomain,
          cancelled_at: account.cancelled_at,
          created_at: account.created_at,
          updated_at: account.updated_at
        }
      end

      def serialize_portal(account)
        {
          name: account.name,
          subdomain: account.subdomain
        }
      end

      def serialize_user(user)
        {
          id: user.id,
          account_id: user.account_id,
          name: user.name,
          email: user.email,
          role: user.role,
          verified: user.verified?,
          verified_at: user.verified_at,
          suspended: user.suspended,
          created_at: user.created_at,
          updated_at: user.updated_at
        }
      end

      def serialize_invitation(invitation)
        {
          id: invitation.id,
          account_id: invitation.account_id,
          invited_by_id: invitation.invited_by_id,
          email: invitation.email,
          role: invitation.role,
          status: invitation.status,
          expires_at: invitation.expires_at,
          accepted_at: invitation.accepted_at,
          revoked_at: invitation.revoked_at,
          created_at: invitation.created_at,
          updated_at: invitation.updated_at
        }
      end

      def serialize_invitation_preview(invitation)
        account = invitation.account
        {
          email: invitation.email,
          role: invitation.role,
          account_name: account.name,
          subdomain: account.subdomain,
          expires_at: invitation.expires_at,
          account: {
            name: account.name,
            subdomain: account.subdomain
          }
        }
      end

      def serialize_session(session, raw_token)
        {
          id: session.id,
          token: raw_token,
          created_at: session.created_at,
          updated_at: session.updated_at
        }
      end

      def serialize_request(ticket)
        {
          id: ticket.id,
          subject: ticket.subject,
          status: ticket.status,
          requester_id: ticket.requester_id,
          created_at: ticket.created_at,
          updated_at: ticket.public_updated_at
        }
      end

      def serialize_ticket(ticket)
        {
          id: ticket.id,
          subject: ticket.subject,
          status: ticket.status,
          requester_id: ticket.requester_id,
          requester: {
            id: ticket.requester.id,
            name: ticket.requester.name,
            email: ticket.requester.email
          },
          assignee_id: ticket.assignee_id,
          assignee: ticket.assignee ? {
            id: ticket.assignee.id,
            name: ticket.assignee.name
          } : nil,
          created_at: ticket.created_at,
          updated_at: ticket.updated_at
        }
      end

      def serialize_comment(comment)

          body: comment.body,
          public: comment.public,
          author: {
            id: comment.author.id,
            name: comment.author.name

      end
    end
  end

    class SessionsController < BaseController
      skip_before_action :require_authentication!, only: :create

        attrs = params.require(:session).permit(:email, :password)
        email = attrs[:email].to_s.strip.downcase
        password = attrs[:password].to_s

        user = current_account.users.find_by(email: email)
        unless user&.authenticate(password)
          return render json: { error: "Invalid email or password" }, status: :unauthorized
        end

        unless user.verified?
          return render json: { error: "Email not verified" }, status: :forbidden
        end

        if user.suspended?
          return render json: { error: "Account is suspended" }, status: :forbidden
        end

        if current_account.cancelled?
          if !user.admin?
            return render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
          elsif current_account.cancellation_expired?
            return render json: { error: "Account cancellation period has expired" }, status: :forbidden
          end
        end

        session, raw_token = Session.issue_for!(user)

        render json: {
          session: serialize_session(session, raw_token),
          user: serialize_user(user),
          account: serialize_account(current_account)
        }, status: :created
      end

      def destroy
        current_session.destroy!
        head :no_content
      end

            errors: ticket.errors.to_hash

        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do

          comment&.save!
        end
        ticket.reload

module Api
  module V1
    class InvitationsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_admin!

      def index
        scope = current_account.invitations.by_id

        if params[:status].present?
          scope = case params[:status].to_s
                  when "pending" then scope.pending
                  when "accepted" then scope.accepted
                  when "revoked" then scope.revoked
                  when "expired" then scope.expired
                  else scope.none
                  end
        end

        records, meta = paginate(scope)
        render json: { invitations: records.map { |invitation| serialize_invitation(invitation) } }.merge(meta), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        invitation = current_account.invitations.find(params[:id])
        render json: { invitation: serialize_invitation(invitation) }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        attrs = params.require(:invitation).permit(:email, :role)
        raw_token, token_digest = Invitation.generate_token

        invitation = current_account.invitations.build(
          invited_by: current_user,
          email: attrs[:email],
          role: attrs[:role],
          token_digest: token_digest,
          expires_at: Time.current + Invitation::TTL
        )

        saved = false
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          current_account.lock!
          if invitation.valid?
            invitation.save!
            saved = true
          end
        end

        unless saved
          return render json: {
            error: invitation.errors.full_messages.first,
            errors: invitation.errors.to_hash
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        UserMailer.invitation(invitation, raw_token).deliver_now

        render json: { invitation: serialize_invitation(invitation) }, status: :created
      end

      def resend
        invitation = current_account.invitations.find(params[:id])

        if invitation.accepted?
          return render json: { error: "Invitation has already been accepted" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        if invitation.revoked?
          return render json: { error: "Invitation has been revoked" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        raw_token = nil
        conflict_error = nil

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          current_account.lock!
          invitation.reload
          if invitation.accepted?
            conflict_error = "Invitation has already been accepted"
          elsif invitation.revoked?
            conflict_error = "Invitation has been revoked"
          elsif current_account.users.exists?(email: invitation.email)
            conflict_error = "Email has already been taken"
          elsif current_account.invitations.pending.where(email: invitation.email).where.not(id: invitation.id).exists?
            conflict_error = "Email already has a pending invitation"
          else
            raw_token = invitation.reissue!
          end
        end

        if conflict_error
          return render json: { error: conflict_error }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        UserMailer.invitation(invitation, raw_token).deliver_now

        render json: { invitation: serialize_invitation(invitation) }, status: :ok
      end

      def destroy
        invitation = current_account.invitations.find(params[:id])

        if invitation.accepted?
          return render json: { error: "Cannot revoke an accepted invitation" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        if invitation.revoked?
          return render json: { error: "Invitation has already been revoked" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        invitation.revoke!
        render json: { invitation: serialize_invitation(invitation) }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end
end

    class UsersController < BaseController
      before_action :require_admin!

      def index
        scope = current_account.users.by_id

        if params[:role].present?
          scope = scope.where(role: params[:role].to_s)
        end

        if params.key?(:suspended) && params[:suspended].to_s != ""
          suspended_val = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(params[:suspended])
          scope = scope.where(suspended: suspended_val)
        end

        records, meta = paginate(scope)
        render json: { users: records.map { |user| serialize_user(user) } }.merge(meta), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        user = current_account.users.find(params[:id])
        render json: { user: serialize_user(user) }, status: :ok
      end

      def update
        user = current_account.users.find(params[:id])
        attrs = params.require(:user).permit(:name, :role, :suspended)

        if attrs.key?(:suspended) && attrs[:suspended].nil?
          return render json: {
            error: "Suspended is invalid",
            errors: { suspended: [ "is not included in the list" ] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        user.assign_attributes(attrs)
        unless user.valid?
          return render json: {
            error: user.errors.full_messages.first,
            errors: user.errors.to_hash
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        last_admin_error = false
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          current_account.lock!
          user.reload
          user.assign_attributes(attrs)

          was_active_admin = user.role_was == "admin" && !user.suspended_was
          still_active_admin = user.role == "admin" && !user.suspended?

          if was_active_admin && !still_active_admin
            other_active_admins = current_account.users.where(role: "admin", suspended: false).where.not(id: user.id).exists?
            unless other_active_admins
              last_admin_error = true
              raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
            end
          end

          newly_suspended = user.suspended_changed? && user.suspended?
          demoted_from_staff = user.role_changed? && !user.staff?

          user.save!

          if newly_suspended
            user.revoke_sessions!
            current_account.tickets.where(assignee_id: user.id).update_all(assignee_id: nil)
          elsif demoted_from_staff
            current_account.tickets.where(assignee_id: user.id).update_all(assignee_id: nil)
          end
        end

        if last_admin_error
          return render json: {
            error: "Cannot suspend the last active admin",
            errors: { suspended: [ "cannot suspend the last active admin" ] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        render json: { user: serialize_user(user) }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class InvitationsTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @acme = create_verified_account(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    @beta = create_verified_account(name: "Beta", subdomain: "beta", admin_name: "Bo", email: "bo@beta.test", password: "beta-first-password")
    @admin_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    @beta_admin_token = sign_in(subdomain: "beta", email: "bo@beta.test", password: "beta-first-password")
  end

  test "admin invites agent, preview and acceptance flow, and immediate sign-in" do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear

    post "/api/v1/invitations",
         params: { invitation: { email: "  Sam@Example.Test ", role: "agent" } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :created

    inv = json_body["invitation"]
    assert_not_nil inv["id"]
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", inv["email"]
    assert_equal "agent", inv["role"]
    assert_equal "pending", inv["status"]
    assert_not_nil inv["expires_at"]
    assert_nil inv["accepted_at"]
    assert_nil inv["revoked_at"]
    assert_nil inv["token_digest"]

    assert_equal 1, ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_equal [ "sam@example.test" ], mail.to
    token = extract_token_from_email(mail)
    assert_includes mail.text_part.body.decoded, "http://localhost:3001/accept-invitation?account=acme&token=#{token}"

    # Preview returns invited email, role, business name, subdomain, expiry
    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
         params: { invitation_preview: { token: token } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    preview = json_body["invitation_preview"]
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", preview["email"]
    assert_equal "agent", preview["role"]
    assert_equal "Acme", preview["account_name"]
    assert_equal "acme", preview["subdomain"]
    assert_equal "Acme", preview.dig("account", "name")
    assert_equal "acme", preview.dig("account", "subdomain")
    assert_not_nil preview["expires_at"]

    # Wrong tenant cannot preview or accept
    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
         params: { invitation_preview: { token: token } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "beta" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
         params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: token, name: "Sam", password: "my-team-password" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "beta" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Short password rejected without consuming invitation
    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
         params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: token, name: "Sam", password: "short" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert json_body["errors"].present?

    # Valid acceptance creates verified user and returns user + account
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
         params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: token, name: "Sam", password: "my-team-password" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal 0, ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size
    assert_equal "Sam", json_body.dig("user", "name")
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", json_body.dig("user", "email")
    assert_equal "agent", json_body.dig("user", "role")
    assert_equal true, json_body.dig("user", "verified")
    assert_equal false, json_body.dig("user", "suspended")
    assert_equal "Acme", json_body.dig("account", "name")
    assert_equal "acme", json_body.dig("account", "subdomain")

    # Token cannot be reused for preview or acceptance
    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
         params: { invitation_preview: { token: token } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
         params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: token, name: "Sam 2", password: "my-team-password" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Sam can sign in immediately without verification email
    sam_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@example.test", password: "my-team-password")
    assert_not_nil sam_token

    # Invitation now shows status=accepted
    get "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv['id']}", headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "accepted", json_body.dig("invitation", "status")
    assert_not_nil json_body.dig("invitation", "accepted_at")

    # Agent cannot access invitation management routes
    get "/api/v1/invitations", headers: auth_headers("acme", sam_token)
    assert_response :forbidden

    post "/api/v1/invitations",
         params: { invitation: { email: "other@example.test", role: "agent" } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", sam_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "competing invitations, customer registration block, resend, revoke, expiration, and listing/filtering" do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear

    # Invite first agent
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
         params: { invitation: { email: "sam@example.test", role: "agent" } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    inv1_id = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")
    token1 = extract_token_from_email(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last)

    # Cannot create competing pending invitation for same email
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
         params: { invitation: { email: "SAM@example.test", role: "admin" } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Cannot invite existing user
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
         params: { invitation: { email: "jo@acme.test", role: "admin" } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Cannot invite customer role
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
         params: { invitation: { email: "cust@example.test", role: "customer" } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Customer registration cannot take pending invite's email on acme
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
         params: { user: { name: "Sam Impostor", email: "SAM@example.test", password: "customer-password" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Customer registration CAN take that email on beta (tenant isolated)
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
         params: { user: { name: "Sam Beta", email: "sam@example.test", password: "customer-password" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "beta" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :created

    # Resend replaces old token
    post "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv1_id}/resend",
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    token2 = extract_token_from_email(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last)
    assert_not_equal token1, token2

    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
         params: { invitation_preview: { token: token1 } },

         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",

         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },

    assert_response :created
    inv4_id = json_body.dig("invitation", "id")

    # Expire inv2 by travelling 8 days forward (inv4 also created at same time, so expire inv2 explicitly for distinct statuses)
    Invitation.find(inv2_id).update!(expires_at: 1.minute.ago)

    # Expired token fails preview and acceptance
    post "/api/v1/invitation_previews",
         params: { invitation_preview: { token: inv2_token } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Listing invitations ordered by ID ascending
    get "/api/v1/invitations", headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ inv1_id, inv2_id, inv3_id, inv4_id ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }

    # Filtering by status
    get "/api/v1/invitations?status=revoked", headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ inv1_id ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/invitations?status=expired", headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ inv2_id ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/invitations?status=accepted", headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ inv3_id ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/invitations?status=pending", headers: auth_headers("acme", @admin_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ inv4_id ], json_body["invitations"].map { |i| i["id"] }

    # Customer registration CAN take expired invite's email
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
         params: { user: { name: "Sam Customer", email: "sam@example.test", password: "customer-password" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :created

    # Cross-tenant show/resend/revoke return 404
    get "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv4_id}", headers: auth_headers("beta", @beta_admin_token)
    assert_response :not_found
    post "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv4_id}/resend", headers: auth_headers("beta", @beta_admin_token)
    assert_response :not_found
    delete "/api/v1/invitations/#{inv4_id}", headers: auth_headers("beta", @beta_admin_token)
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  private

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)
    {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}"
    }
  end
end

class UsersAndStaffTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do

    @avery = @acme.users.create!(name: "Avery Customer", email: "avery@example.test", password: "cust-password-123", role: "customer", verified_at: Time.current)

    @bo = @beta.users.find_by!(email: "bo@beta.test")

    @jo_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    @pat_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "pat@acme.test", password: "admin-password-123")
    @sam_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@acme.test", password: "agent-password-123")
    @avery_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "cust-password-123")
    @bo_token = sign_in(subdomain: "beta", email: "bo@beta.test", password: "beta-first-password")
  end

  test "admin lists, filters, inspects users, and staff endpoint supplies active staff by ID ascending" do
    # List all users ordered by ID ascending
    get "/api/v1/users", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @jo.id, @pat.id, @sam.id, @avery.id ], json_body["users"].map { |u| u["id"] }
    assert_equal [ false, false, false, false ], json_body["users"].map { |u| u["suspended"] }

    # Filter by role
    get "/api/v1/users?role=admin", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @jo.id, @pat.id ], json_body["users"].map { |u| u["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/users?role=agent", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @sam.id ], json_body["users"].map { |u| u["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/users?role=customer", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "Sam Agent", json_body.dig("user", "name")

    # Cross-tenant user access -> 404
    get "/api/v1/users/#{@sam.id}", headers: auth_headers("beta", @bo_token)
    assert_response :not_found

    # Agent and customer cannot manage users
    get "/api/v1/users", headers: auth_headers("acme", @sam_token)
    assert_response :forbidden
    get "/api/v1/users/#{@sam.id}", headers: auth_headers("acme", @sam_token)
    assert_response :forbidden
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{@avery.id}", params: { user: { suspended: true } }, headers: auth_headers("acme", @sam_token), as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden

    get "/api/v1/users", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)
    assert_response :forbidden

    # GET /staff accessible to both admin and agent, forbidden to customer
    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @jo.id, @pat.id, @sam.id ], json_body["staff"].map { |u| u["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: auth_headers("acme", @sam_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @jo.id, @pat.id, @sam.id ], json_body["staff"].map { |u| u["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)
    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "suspension revokes sessions, clears assignments, updates staff list, and protects last active admin" do
    # Create a ticket assigned to Sam
    post "/api/v1/requests",
         params: { request: { subject: "Help me", comment: { body: "Details" } } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    ticket_id = json_body.dig("request", "id")

    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
          params: { ticket: { assignee_id: @sam.id } },
          headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @sam.id, json_body.dig("ticket", "assignee_id")

    # Suspend Sam
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{@sam.id}",
          params: { user: { suspended: true } },
          headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal true, json_body.dig("user", "suspended")

    # Sam's existing session is revoked
    get "/api/v1/me", headers: auth_headers("acme", @sam_token)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    # Sam cannot sign in while suspended
    post "/api/v1/sessions",
         params: { session: { email: "sam@acme.test", password: "agent-password-123" } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
         as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden

    # Ticket assignment cleared
    get "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_nil json_body.dig("ticket", "assignee_id")
    assert_nil json_body.dig("ticket", "assignee")

    # Staff list excludes suspended Sam
    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @jo.id, @pat.id ], json_body["staff"].map { |u| u["id"] }

    # Filter users by suspension
    get "/api/v1/users?suspended=true", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @sam.id ], json_body["users"].map { |u| u["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/users?suspended=false", headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @jo.id, @pat.id, @avery.id ], json_body["users"].map { |u| u["id"] }

    # Suspend Pat (Jo is still active admin -> succeeds)
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{@pat.id}",
          params: { user: { suspended: true } },
          headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal true, json_body.dig("user", "suspended")

    get "/api/v1/me", headers: auth_headers("acme", @pat_token)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    # Now Jo is the last active admin -> cannot suspend Jo
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{@jo.id}",
          params: { user: { suspended: true } },
          headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal false, @jo.reload.suspended?

    # Cannot demote last active admin either
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{@jo.id}",
          params: { user: { role: "agent" } },
          headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "admin", @jo.reload.role

    # Unsuspend Sam -> Sam can sign in and appears in /staff again
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{@sam.id}",
          params: { user: { suspended: false } },
          headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal false, json_body.dig("user", "suspended")

    new_sam_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@acme.test", password: "agent-password-123")
    assert_not_nil new_sam_token

    get "/api/v1/staff", headers: auth_headers("acme", new_sam_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ @jo.id, @sam.id ], json_body["staff"].map { |u| u["id"] }
  end

  private

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)
    {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}"
    }
  end
end

class TicketsAssignmentAndInternalActivityTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest

    @avery = @acme.users.create!(name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: "cust-password-123", role: "customer", verified_at: Time.current)

    @beta = create_verified_account(name: "Beta", subdomain: "beta", admin_name: "Bo", email: "bo@beta.test", password: "beta-first-password")

    @avery_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "cust-password-123")
  end

  test "staff assigns and clears ticket assignee, validates assignee constraints" do
    post "/api/v1/requests",
         params: { request: { subject: "Need help", comment: { body: "Please assist" } } },
         headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :created

    assert_nil json_body.dig("ticket", "assignee_id")

          as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    assert_equal @sam.id, json_body["tickets"].first["assignee_id"]
    assert_equal({ "id" => @sam.id, "name" => "Sam Agent" }, json_body["tickets"].first["assignee"])

    # Invalid assignees rejected (customer, suspended staff, cross-tenant staff, nonexistent)
    [ @avery.id, @suspended_agent.id, @bo.id, 999_999 ].each do |bad_id|
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
            params: { ticket: { assignee_id: bad_id } },
            headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
            as: :json
      assert_response :unprocessable_entity
      assert_equal @sam.id, Ticket.find(ticket_id).assignee_id

          params: { ticket: { assignee_id: nil } },

          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_nil json_body.dig("ticket", "assignee_id")
    assert_nil json_body.dig("ticket", "assignee")
  end

  test "internal activity (assignment and private notes) does not change customer-facing request" do

    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-10 10:00:00 UTC") do

           params: { request: { subject: "First", comment: { body: "First body" } } },

    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-10 10:01:00 UTC") do

           headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token),

      r2 = json_body["request"]

    assert_equal [ r2["id"], r1["id"] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

            headers: auth_headers("acme", @sam_token),

    get "/api/v1/requests/#{r1['id']}", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)

    get "/api/v1/requests", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r2["id"], r1["id"] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r1["id"], r2["id"] ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal [ true, false ], json_body["comments"].map { |c| c["public"] }
    assert_equal [ "First body", "Checking this with billing." ], json_body["comments"].map { |c| c["body"] }

    # Clearing assignment via user suspension also does not change customer-facing request
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-10 10:06:00 UTC") do
      patch "/api/v1/users/#{@sam.id}",
            params: { user: { suspended: true } },
            headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
            as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    get "/api/v1/requests/#{r1['id']}", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal r1, json_body["request"]

    get "/api/v1/requests", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r2["id"], r1["id"] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

    # Public reply on r1 DOES update customer-facing request and ordering
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-10 10:07:00 UTC") do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{r1['id']}",
            params: { ticket: { comment: { body: "Here is an update for you.", public: true } } },
            headers: auth_headers("acme", @jo_token),
            as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    get "/api/v1/requests", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r1["id"], r2["id"] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests/#{r1['id']}", headers: auth_headers("acme", @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_not_equal r1["updated_at"], json_body.dig("request", "updated_at")
  end

  private

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)
    {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}"
    }
  end
end
